title: Field Counsel — LLM API Scenario Pocket Guide
content:
Purpose: Fast, jaw-pocket reference for sales reps and AE technical presales when engaging buyers comparing Redwood Inference vs generic LLM API providers. Focus: scenarios, short scripts, traps, and quick technical counters reps can use without deep engineering back-and-forth.

How to use: Scan for the buyer scenario that matches the call signal; use the core response + tactical script verbatim, then follow the Close Motions. If an engineering deep-dive is requested, pick the relevant technical appendix lines.

Key principles (2 lines to keep front of mind):
- Emphasize operational predictability: throughput, latency SLOs, and rollout controls beat bench-top model quality conversations in closing cycles.
- Move from abstract to concrete: cost-per-100k tokens, tail-latency percentiles (p95/p99), and a migration/fallback plan.

Scenario Matrix (quick lookup)
1) Startup PLG POC — "We just need a fast chat demo, cheapest way to ship."
   - Customer signal: single microservice, <1M tokens/mo expected, fast time-to-prototype.
   - Typical objection: "We can just use CloudX/Generic API — it's cheaper and faster to start."
   - Core response: Redwood reduces unit costs at scale while letting you ship quickly (hosted API) and then transition to Dedicated when committed throughput matters.
   - Tactical script: "Totally — CloudX is great for first hour prototypes. Redwood gets you from prototype to predictable production without refactoring: same SDK, pin versions, and an easy Dedicated upgrade path if you need steady SLOs or lower unit cost. I can show a migration checklist in 15 minutes."
   - Close motions: Offer a 30-day POC credit + migration checklist doc; schedule a 15-min tech touch after demo.

2) Enterprise regulated-data use case — "Data residency + audit logs required."
   - Signal: legal/regulatory requirement for VPC, KMS, or on-prem.
   - Typical objection: "Public API vendors can't meet our compliance requirements."
   - Core response: Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) is designed for those constraints, with audit logs and KMS integrations. We also support private control plane deployments with SOC2 and enterprise support.
   - Tactical script: "We treat compliance as a primary product problem — we ship Private deployments with your KMS and audit retention profiles. If you need an air-gapped option, we have a path and professional services for the initial rollout."
   - Close motions: Offer a demo of Private deployment architecture + reference from an existing regulated customer.

3) Latency-critical product feature — "Search UI / real-time chat must be snappy."
   - Signal: p95/p99 latency concerns, UX constraints, synchronous frontend calls.
   - Typical objection: "CloudX API is already fast — why switch?"
   - Core response: Redwood’s serving runtime and smart routing focus on tail latency and predictable p95/p99 — plus caching and KV prefix reuse to shave tens to hundreds of ms.
   - Tactical script: "We measure and optimize for p95/p99 in production, not just average latency. For similar models, our runtime and caching often cut tail latency by 20–40% under load. If you share your 95th/99th target, we can propose a config that meets it within the first week."
   - Close motions: Offer a latency SLO draft and a short benchmarking plan (synthetic & replay).

4) Cost-sensitive embedding/batch workloads — "Embeddings are expensive at scale."
   - Signal: large corpus, repeated reruns, or vector store costs ballooning.
   - Typical objection: "API pricing is cheaper elsewhere for bulk embeddings."
   - Core response: Redwood Optimize and intelligent caching/batch tooling reduce token and compute cost. Dedicated or quantized private deployments further lower per-unit spend.
   - Tactical script: "We built optimized embedding pipelines and cache layers — many customers see 2–5x reduction in per-embedding cost after applying DeltaCacher and batching guidance. Let's run a quick sample run on a canonical 100k row set."
   - Close motions: Offer cost projection spreadsheet and a joint pilot for 2–3 embedding strategies.

Trap Lines and High-Risk Questions (and how to defuse them)
- "Will Redwood lock us into a proprietary SDK?" — Answer: "No — same open protocols and well-documented SDKs, plus exportable model artifacts and clear migration docs. The control plane-related features are additive operationally, not vendor-locking."
- "How do we know your reported latency numbers aren't synthetic?" — Answer: "We publish sample workloads and an anonymized SLO dataset. We also run replayed traces from customer-like workloads during POC; we'll include that in the benchmarking plan."
- "What happens if you have an outage?" — Answer: "We design for graceful degradation: automated fallbacks to compatible models/regions and can configure local caches or a standby Dedicated pool for critical routes. We document RTO/RPO in enterprise contracts."
- "Why not run open-source on our infra?" — Answer: "You can — Redwood Private provides the same operational primitives without building the stack (autoscaling, kernel tuning, KV cache, rollout mechanics), so your team avoids repeated SRE/infra cycles and faster time-to-value."

Rapid Rebuttals (one-liners to interrupt negotiation drift)
- Pricing FUD: "Unit price is one data point — predictability of spend (commits, burst policies) and engineering hours to operate matter far more over 3–12 months."
- Feature FUD: "We match or exceed feature parity for hosted APIs; where we differ is in ops tooling (tracing, per-route budgets, safe rollouts)."
- Open source bragging: "Open models are great; Redwood's value is making them operational at scale without repeated SRE cycles."

Technical Appendix (quick reference lines to memorize)
- Typical p95/p99 numbers: hosted median p95 ~80–140ms for 8k context gen (depends on model); p99 ~150–400ms; Dedicated gets tighter SLOs depending on commit.
- Pricing flavors to call out: per-token hosted tiers, reserved capacity (monthly/annual) vs usage, add-ons (observability retention, compliance).
- Rollout primitives: canary percentage, A/B route split, automatic fallback to a cheaper compatible model. Mention that these are controllable per-route in the Console.
- Integrations: KMS/HSM, SSO (SAML/OIDC), SIEM forwarding for audit logs, vector store connectors.

Playbook snippets (short scripts to paste into Slack/email)
- Quick follow-up email after discovery: "Thanks for the call — based on latency and compliance signals, I recommend a two-phase approach: (1) Hosted POC to validate quality/UX, (2) Private/Dedicated design + cost projection for scale. I'll attach a migration checklist and proposed benchmark plan. When can we schedule 15m with your infra lead?"
- Engineering nudge for benchmarking: "Share a 5–10 minute trace and a small sample of your payloads and we'll replay it against our hosted runtime and show the delta for p95/p99 and cost. No code changes required."

Reference edges (when to escalate to Solutions Engineering)
- If a customer requires an air-gapped install, escalate immediately (SE + Professional Services).
- If they demand sub-50ms p95 for a 4k-context gen under load, schedule a joint benchmark (SRE + Serving runtime) — this is specialized tuning.
- If legal requests custom contract language for data residency, loop in Legal and Security for a tailored Private deployment term sheet.

Open questions / follow-ups to track (internal)
- Build a short sample benchmark kit (synthetic + small replay) for field use — GH issue created: GH: redwood-inference/field-playbook#98.
- Add 2–3 regulator-focused reference customers to the sales collateral library.
- Create a one-page Private-deployment checklist for AEs to attach to Enterprise proposals.

Notes: Keep this doc lean and update monthly. If a new repeated objection appears in deals, add it as a new scenario.

Prepared by: Ben Kline (GTM). Last updated: 2025-03-03.
